RISP ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT STATEMENT
A. Description of the Proposed Action
The scientific objectives of the Ross Ice Shelf Project (RISP) are to investigate the physical, chemical, biological, and geological conditions in the ice shelf, in the water mass beneath the shelf, and in the soft sediments and bedrock at the bottom of the sea, and to use the data obtained in the interpretation of the present conditions and the past history of this portion of Antarctica.
The prime requisite for the achievement of these objectives is the development of a drilling system that will penetrate the ice shelf. The success of the Ross Ice Shelf Project will depend upon the ability to obtain ice cores and to open and maintain access holes that will allow sampling of the water column, investigation of the ice-water and water-sediment interfaces, collection of aquatic biota, and sampling of the sub-sea sediments. It has become clear that the relatively modest investment in the equipment required for drilling these holes will provide the possibility for a broad range of new and important investigations with results which will bear not only on questions which may be unique to the Antarctic but more important, which will bear on questions of hemispheric and worldwide significance.
